sections.description: This section outlines the patient’s presenting complaints, physical findings, and early investigations that guided the differential diagnosis. It emphasizes the atypical features of neck swelling in dermatomyositis and the importance of a systematic bedside examination in emergency and ENT settings.
subtopics: History of neck swelling, proximal weakness, and myalgia
Physical examination: neck edema, facial erythema, nailfold changes, and musculoskeletal signs
Differential considerations: Ludwig’s angina, idiopathic angioedema, infection vs. autoimmune causes
Early imaging (CT neck) and lab work (CRP, WCC, CK, transaminases)
Red flags prompting reconsideration of initial diagnoses

sections.description: This section explains the logical pathway from suspicion to definitive diagnosis, integrating clinical features with laboratory, imaging, and histopathology findings specific to dermatomyositis and anti‑SAE1 antibody positivity.
subtopics: Key clinical red flags for inflammatory myopathy
Role of creatine kinase and inflammatory markers
Autoantibody testing: ANA, myositis panel, SAE1 specificity
Complement and angioedema work‑up (C1 esterase, C3/C4)
Muscle imaging: MRI, FDG‑PET patterns
Muscle biopsy findings: perifascicular necrosis, MHC‑Ia, C5b‑9 deposition
Correlating skin manifestations (Holster sign, periungual erythema) with systemic disease

sections.description: This section details the rationale behind each therapeutic intervention, the sequence of escalation, and the considerations for avoiding drug‑specific adverse events in a patient with respiratory involvement.
subtopics: High‑dose IV methylprednisolone and taper schedule
Adjunctive immunosuppressants: mycophenolate mofetil, rituximab, IVIG
Avoiding methotrexate in context of lung disease
Pneumocystis prophylaxis options and management of haemolytic anaemia
Monitoring for immunosuppressant toxicity and drug interactions
Feeding and dysphagia management (NG tube, swallow therapy)
Multidisciplinary coordination (ENT, rheumatology, pulmonology, nutrition)

sections.description: This section reviews the patient’s trajectory from acute hospitalization to remission, outlines objective outcome measures, and discusses ongoing surveillance for relapse, organ involvement, and malignancy.
subtopics: Short‑term recovery: CK normalization, muscle strength, edema resolution
Long‑term remission milestones (prednisone discontinuation, dysphagia resolution)
Pulmonary function and imaging follow‑up for aspiration‑related changes
Risk assessment for occult malignancy (IMACS guidelines, high‑risk profile)
Surveillance plan: imaging, tumor markers, endoscopic evaluations
Role of maintenance IVIG and tapering mycophenolate
Patient education and self‑monitoring for disease activity

sections.description: This concise section distills key take‑aways for clinicians, highlighting diagnostic pitfalls, the spectrum of dermatomyositis presentations, and evidence‑based treatment principles for anti‑SAE1 cases.
subtopics: Endoscopic appearance of neck edema: distinguishing angioedema from myositis‑related swelling
Value of early CK measurement in unexplained soft‑tissue swelling
Recognizing subtle cutaneous signs when rash is absent
Importance of autoantibody profiling in guiding therapy intensity
Balancing immunosuppression with organ‑specific considerations (lung disease)
Documentation of multidisciplinary care pathways in complex autoimmune cases
